section_readTheCommit.whatItChanges: On-roll accounts whose CAD situsAddress is punctuation-only were previously `continue`d past in the conformant bake's per-row loop before any database write, freezing them on their pre-conformant snapshot forever. The fix writes the row with an earned absence on baseFacts.situsAddress (verdict absent-verified, basis quoting the raw offending punctuation value) instead of discarding the rest of the row's facts. situsCity/situsZip remain decided independently (unchanged mechanism); a genuinely blank (never guard-refused) claim still bakes a bare null, byte-identical to today. PUNCTUATION_ONLY_RE and assertSitusNotPunctuationOnly (the guard itself) are untouched. skippedBadSitus is renamed situsPunctuationOnlyAbsence and now also logged per-county to stdout, not only the tail JSON summary. A new assertSitusAddressAbsenceEarned fails closed on a malformed absence object or a basis that doesn't name the parcel, the same shape as assertRequiredLeafStatesEarned.

section_bakeReachability_designForTheTra.priorFalseClaimBeingGuardedAgainst: The last pin bump (CTX-MIRROR, pinned by an earlier integration-seat claim) asserted 69de8fe6 was urgent because the bake was behind the serve. CTX-BUILD measured that false: Dockerfile.publish copies only /ldt/node_modules and /app/bakes, and /app/bakes is an esbuild bundle over a fixed set of entrypoints; 69de8fe6's two changed files sat outside that graph entirely.
section_bakeReachability_designForTheTra.methodChosen: An independent Node script (not esbuild itself, to avoid needing a full pnpm install of LDT's workspace just to resolve the bundle) that recursively follows only relative (./ ../) import/export/require specifiers from a set of entrypoint files -- exactly the specifiers esbuild inlines into a bundle when bundle:true and the target is not marked external. Bare/package specifiers are recorded as external leaves and not expanded, matching the EXTERNAL list in scripts/build-publish-bake-clis.mjs (pg, sharp, @google-cloud/*, etc. are never going to be in 'our' graph regardless).
section_bakeReachability_designForTheTra.validationBeforeTrust: Before running the tracer against the new commit, it was run against the OLD pin (3885efad) with the four entrypoints CTX-BUILD's own comment names, to see whether it reproduces CTX-BUILD's already-trusted claimed result (26 modules, 0 unresolved relative specifiers) before being trusted on anything new. It reproduced that result exactly, module list included. This is the adversarial check for CP1: a tracer that cannot reproduce a known answer is not a tracer, it is a guess.
